newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds see Italy debut in French francs.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds see Italy debut in French francs.

text.p: The highlight of the Wednesday morning Eurobond session was Italy's 5.0 billion French franc 10-year bond, its first transaction in that currency.
The deal, priced to yield 18 basis points over OATs, quickly sold out and was hailed a success by market players.
"The bond was a big success," an official at joint lead manager CDC Marches said.

"We sold out of the bonds, and placed it with a wide range of investors, including many outside France. European investors have not been strong buyers of Franc bonds recently, but were attracted by the quality of the deal and its rarity," he said.
The paper had traded slightly tighter by 1120 GMT, and traders said the spread could come in by around one b.p. today.
Bankers said similar transaction from Portugal and Spain were trading at around 18 and 15 b.p. over OATs respectively. Italy could trade below that level over time, they said.
"We have seen a lot of interest in the bond, and placed paper with French buyers and in Italy too," a rival Paris-based Eurobond specialist said.
"The deal is trading at the reoffer price -- its a very good deal," he said.
The bond is a latest in a series of benchmark transactions Italy has issued in key European currencies, as part of a drive to familiarise European investors with its credit ahead of monetary union.

"Italy wants to create a benchmark is all the major European currencies," an official at joint lead manager J.P. Morgan said. "It has already tapped guilders, Swiss francs and Ecu so French francs was the next step."

The dollar sector, the main focus of primary market activity in recent weeks, saw further supply. WestLB, BremerLB and LB Schleswig Holstein all issued short-dated opportunistic deals, aimed at retail investors.
Bankers said the transactions were ordinary, but more interesting institutional-targeted business was unlikely to surface until next week.
"We expect a bit of a lull in dollars over the coming days, but a number of borrowers are eyeing sizeable five-year dollar deals for next week," a syndicate manager at a U.S. bank said.

On the emerging market side, Philippine company Benpres Holdings issued a $150 million December 2002 bond at around 155 b.p. over Treasuries via J.P. Morgan. Dealers said most of the paper was placed in Asia.
Votorantim added to recent supply from Brazil by launching a $400 million bond, to be priced later to yield 210 b.p. over U.S. Treasury notes.
